newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland boosts intervention diesel reserves sales.
newsitem.headline: Poland boosts intervention diesel reserves sales.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday decided to boost to 45,000 tonnes from 30,000 tonnes the amount of diesel fuel offered from state reserves at its weekly intervention auctions, the deputy industry minister said.
"We have decided to increase the amount of fuel on offer to 45,000 tonnes...and the first auction will be this week and the following one next week," Roman Czerwinski told a news conference.
He said if the 90,000 tonne offer proved too small to stabilise the market hit by high world oil prices, the cabinet would consider freeing another 150,000 tonnes of diesel.
Last week the government decided to use up to 120,000 tonnes of diesel fuel from the state reserves to cool-down the market by offering the fuel at the weekly auctions.
So far the government sold 31,500 tonnes of diesel at last Wednesday's auction.
Czerwinski said the total amount of freed reserves should be sufficient to meet increased demand for diesel fuel from farmers during the harvest season.
"In the beginning of November demand for diesel should fall and then we will start rebuilding the reserves," he said.
